source_contract.statement: The subscription denial code exists in SkillSubscriptionService but is absent from both message bundles, so ApiResponseFactory falls back to the raw code.
Register exactly one English and one Chinese value for error.skill.subscription.noPermission without changing the exception system.
Both subscriber listeners pass a missing namespace as null to eligibility, and SubscriptionMetadataAccessPolicy denies every account when namespace is null.
Publish and yank subscriber fan-out must each emit a WARN with skillId and namespaceId when namespace is missing, without subscriber identifiers and without changing deny semantics.
For a non-null namespace the recipient sequence and each recipient tuple must be elementwise identical to the frozen behavior.
SkillPublishedEvent reaches owner notification, subscriber notification, and search-index rebuild consumers after confirm-publish makes the event reachable.
Do not prune retained subscription rows in this change; provide a neutral maintainer decision draft under multica-ledger only.
The new English and Chinese message values should exactly match the existing lifecycle permission message style.
Do not modify authorization policy, eligibility, event records or producers, notification payloads, search implementation, database migrations, or workflows.
Publication branch synchronization, PR body mutation, Draft-to-Ready transition, and remote CI readback are not engineering-chain actions.

invariants.statement: A subscription authorization denial remains HTTP 403 but renders a concrete English or Chinese message instead of the raw code.
Adding localization never changes the current-read authorization decision or creates persistence/event side effects on denial.
This change performs no automatic deletion, count rewrite, or readback rewrite for retained subscription rows before maintainer decision.
Retained-row readback is explicitly represented and characterized; if blind review proves unauthorized PRIVATE metadata exposure, the plan returns rather than excluding it as a non-goal.
The owner notification still reaches only the event publisher when publisherId equals the current skill ownerId.
No owner notification recipient or payload changes arise from subscriber null-namespace logging.
A missing namespace yields zero subscriber notification persistence and zero SSE transport in both publish and yank paths.
The new WARN exposes only skillId and namespaceId and never subscriber identifiers, candidate lists, or other user-identifying data.
With a non-null namespace the ordered publish dispatcher tuples are elementwise identical between frozen and candidate trees.
Removed, downgraded, inactive, missing, ordinary PRIVATE, and cross-namespace subscribers remain excluded at event time.
With a non-null namespace the ordered yank dispatcher tuples are elementwise identical between frozen and candidate trees.
Yank notifications still require wasPublished=true and current read eligibility, and still skip the actor.
A committed SkillPublishedEvent still invokes rebuildBySkill for the same skill and indexes current latest metadata.
Portal search does not expose PRIVATE documents and keeps namespace membership, active, hidden, and namespace lifecycle predicates.

work_partition.no_split_rationale: F1 and F2 production files differ, but all six behavior paths share one authorization/event acceptance matrix, one test module, one append-only index tail, and a baseline that must be captured before candidate edits. A single unit prevents baseline contamination and test/index merge conflicts without losing meaningful parallelism.
